winner.title: Mansaf (Spiced Lamb With Rice and Yogurt Sauce)

evidence.authenticity: Traditional jameed-based sauce, lamb shanks, shrak/markook bread, rice with turmeric, toasted almonds. Author Reem Kassis is a Palestinian food writer and cookbook author. Headnote describes Bedouin roots. Small deductions: shanks and Calrose or jasmine rice, where Jordanian cooks usually use shoulder and Egyptian rice.
evidence.precision: Weights for 11 of 21 ingredients (shanks 1.5 kg, onion 226 g, rice 453 g, jameed 1 kg). Sensory cues in 14 steps (very tender but not falling off the bone, sauce consistency between whole milk and half-and-half, whisk constantly to avoid curdling, and a fix if it does). Pan sizes and temperatures are not given.
evidence.testing: Serious Eats editorial process. Explains why to blanch the shanks, why to whisk continuously, why to add cornstarch, and how to rescue curdled sauce. Only 8 ratings (4.3).
evidence.photos: All 11 steps have step images in the schema.
evidence.efficiency: About 2.5 hours total. The sauce and rice are made while the lamb simmers.
evidence.access: Liquid jameed is sold in Tetra Paks (Kasih, Ziyad) at Middle Eastern groceries or online. A reconstitution method for dried jameed discs is given. Shrak and markook are available at Middle Eastern stores, and the page's note gives alternatives.

winner.why: Beat the runner-up with full process photos, gram weights, a doneness cue on nearly every step, and an author from the region.

runnerUp.title: Jordanian Mansaf (Lamb with Jameed)

evidence.authenticity: Lamb shoulder, Egyptian rice, liquid jameed and markook, all traditional. The author is a food blogger and not an authority on Jordanian cooking.
evidence.precision: Weights for 1 of 19 ingredients. 7 sensory cues, no temperatures or pan sizes, and 'large pot' sizing.
evidence.testing: Blogger notes only, with little reasoning. 2 ratings.
evidence.photos: No step images in the schema. 51 images on the page, and I did not confirm they show process stages.
evidence.access: Needs liquid jameed, and the page has notes on it.

runnerUp.why: Fewer weights, no process photos, and a thinner explanation of technique.

notes: Foreign Fork scored 55: weights on 3 of 15 ingredients, no step photos in the schema, and it uses 'maqluba spice'. Saveur scored 52: no author on the page, no process photos, no roots, no jameed substitute. Saveur has a good overnight jameed method but is vague on quantities. Candidate scores for Foreign Fork and Saveur are estimates from the read output. I did not run a full per-criterion breakdown for them. Jameed is the one hard-to-find item, and the winner covers it.
